note: These rooms are samples. Once the nightly run is set up, Claude writes them from your todo list and from what you carved into the stone the day before.

plants.title: The form you keep walking round
plants.instructions: There is a piece of admin you have been circling for weeks. Don't plan all of it. Find the next thing your body has to do: go somewhere, phone someone, print something.
plants.ask: Write that one step, the day, the time, and where you will be. Pick a time you would actually keep.

treasure.name: Brass compass
treasure.description: It points at the next small step, never at the whole journey.

treasure.name: Rubber stamp
treasure.description: APPROVED, it says. Somebody believed it would be.

notes.title: Scratched into the pillar
notes.text: People who write down when and where they will do something follow through far more often than people who only mean to. The if-then planning studies find it again and again.

plants.title: Before the real dig goes further
plants.instructions: There is a sealed passage under the house. Most caves form where slightly acidic water dissolves limestone along cracks, over tens of thousands of years, and a cellar passage can just as easily be something people dug and filled in. Either way, what matters first is what the house is standing on.
plants.ask: Write three questions you would want answered before you dig further, and who could answer each one.

treasure.name: Rock core sample
treasure.description: Banded grey and cream. Somebody drilled for it and never came back.

treasure.name: Carbide lamp
treasure.description: Cavers used these for a hundred years: water dripped on calcium carbide makes a gas that burns bright.

notes.title: Station log, day 3
notes.text: Questions before digging under a building: Is the passage under a load-bearing wall? Is the ground clay, chalk, sandstone or fill? Is there water? A structural engineer can usually answer the first two in one visit.

plants.title: Fifteen minutes outside
plants.instructions: The anxiety will say there isn't time. It says that without evidence. Each walk you write down here is a piece of evidence one way or the other.
plants.ask: When today will you walk, and which way will you go? Write the time and the route.

treasure.name: Golden acorn
treasure.description: Warm in the hand, as if it had been in the sun all day.

treasure.name: Owl feather
treasure.description: Silent flight: the edge is combed so the air makes no sound.

treasure.name: River stone
treasure.description: Smooth on one side, still rough on the other. It isn't finished.

plants.title: Three receipts
plants.instructions: Not what you owe. What went in yesterday: something someone did, something you made, something that was simply good.

treasure.name: Ice lantern
treasure.description: A candle inside a shell of ice. It lasts longer than you would think.

treasure.name: Old tooth
treasure.description: From something big. It lost it a long time ago and was fine.

notes.title: On a frozen signpost
notes.text: Writing down three good things each evening was one of the exercises in Seligman's 2005 study. Its effect showed up over weeks, not in a day.
